2608.06931.title: Science Edge Evaluation: SEE the Missing Step Toward Real Scientific Discovery
2608.06931.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly involved in scientific discovery, yet it remains unclear whether they can support complex real laboratory science. Here we introduce Science Edge Evaluation (SEE), a multimodal benchmark of expert-curated questions grounded in peer-reviewed literature and experimental practice in chemistry, biology, and materials science. Evaluation of 19 multimodal large language models (MLLMs) shows that even the best-performing model reaches only 48.7% accuracy. Moreover, general-purpose models outperform science-specialized models on average. In the visual-agent evaluation, the use of tools increases the best accuracy to 52.7%. Tool use can expand the information available to models, but more information does not necessarily lead to reliable scientific reasoning. The key challenge is whether models can manage tool-derived information within the boundaries of the original experimental evidence. Together, these findings reveal that current MLLMs still cannot reliably make justified and evidence-bounded inferences from experimental results, which is an essential capability in real scientific discovery. Bridging this gap requires MLLMs to transition from explaining established scientific concepts to deriving novel and evidence-based insights from experimental data.
2608.06931.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地參與科學發現，但尚不清楚它們是否能支持複雜的實驗室科學。<lb/>在這裡，我們介紹科學邊緣評估（SEE），這是一個基於同行評審文獻和化學、生物學及材料科學實驗實踐的專家策劃問題的多模態基準。<lb/>對19個多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）的評估顯示，即使是表現最佳的模型，準確率也僅達到48.7%。<lb/>此外，通用模型的表現平均優於專門針對科學的模型。<lb/>在視覺代理評估中，使用工具將最佳準確率提高到52.7%。<lb/>工具的使用可以擴展模型可用的信息，但更多的信息不一定會導致可靠的科學推理。<lb/>關鍵挑戰在於模型是否能在原始實驗證據的範疇內管理工具衍生的信息。<lb/>綜合這些發現顯示，目前的MLLMs仍然無法可靠地從實驗結果中做出有根據且受證據限制的推論，而這在真實的科學發現中是一項基本能力。<lb/>彌補這一差距需要MLLMs從解釋已建立的科學概念轉向從實驗數據中推導出新穎且基於證據的見解。
